prompt: Use case: illustration-story. Asset type: a production atlas of circular illustrated tokens for Creation, an original elemental myth about making a vast living world. The reference is the APPROVED STYLE AND CONTINUITY anchor, not a sheet to copy unchanged. Paint new subjects in exactly that family: luminous opaque gouache, selective fine ink contours, strong simplified silhouettes readable at 64px; deep lapis interiors, jade and turquoise, burnt ochre, muted coral, warm ivory light, very narrow ivory-gold rims. Not glossy coins or flat generic pictograms. Each icon is a complete perfect CIRCLE with opaque painted interior and transparent empty space outside. Center each circle in its own equal grid cell, circle diameter 80 percent of the shorter cell side, generous empty gutters. Absolutely no letters, names, numbers, grid lines, labels, UI, watermark or cast shadows outside circles. No modern laboratory hardware, books, houses or buildings. Only the specified object inside each circle, with a simple dark ground or essential local context. Tiny details must not carry the meaning. Related states should differ in structure, not merely colour. Follow item order exactly, left to right, top to bottom. Exactly 20 circles in 5 columns and 4 rows. Landscape atlas. Exact cell subjects: CELL 1, Flowers: Three simple coral and ochre flowers open on a leafy green stem, with broad petals and visible central pollen-bearing structures. Avoid a cut bouquet or decorative vase. Distinguish: Flower anatomy and attached living plant dominate, without visiting insect, developed fruit or recovery backdrop. CELL 2, Pollination: One six-legged ochre insect bridges two open coral flowers, with a few visible pale pollen grains on its body and on the second flower's centre. Distinguish: Pollen transfer between two flowers is the action; the returning population icon includes young woodland and multiple visitors. CELL 3, Seeds: Three plump ochre seeds lie together, one split to reveal a pale curled plant embryo and its stored food beneath a dark protective coat. Distinguish: Substantial seed bodies and plant embryo, without airborne dust, waiting through seasons or animal egg contents. CELL 4, Seedling: One fresh jade seedling rises from a cracked ochre seed, showing two broad cotyledons above a short stem and a single fine root below. Distinguish: One complete germinating seed with paired seed leaves; green shoots are a survivor group among dead ground. CELL 5, Windborne seeds: Three recognizable ochre seeds carry broad pale papery wings as they spiral away from a leafy branch, each heavy seed body distinct from its wing. Distinguish: Large winged seeds carried by air, not microscopic spores, deposited seeds or bird flight. CELL 6, Fruit: A short living branch carries two plump coral fruits and one opened fruit showing several dark seeds inside its pale flesh. Distinguish: Ripe fleshy seed enclosure isolated as a branch; no recovery woodland or emphasis on a loose seed supply. CELL 7, Seed dispersal: A small four-limbed animal carries a coral fruit away from its parent plant, while two intact dark seeds lie farther along its path on bare soil. Distinguish: Animal movement and separated seeds link fruit to new ground; no dung pile or generalized wind scatter. CELL 8, Flowering forest: Three established green tree crowns carry small coral blossoms and ochre fruit above a shaded floor, with one bird and one small mammal at different branches. Distinguish: Mature flower-and-fruit forest community before catastrophe, without young sapling rows, broken old trunks or giant-free recovery evidence. CELL 9, Axial tilt: The familiar hook-marked planet spins around a single thin ivory axis visibly tilted diagonally against a faint horizontal orbital plane; one short curved stroke circles a pole. Distinguish: One oblique straight axis through one globe, no symmetric field loops or four seasonal views. CELL 10, Seasons: Four small views of the same branch form a loose ring around a golden sun: fresh leaves, full foliage, ochre falling leaves and a bare snow-touched twig. A faint tilted planetary axis anchors the centre. Distinguish: Four changing living states and sunlight, not pebble counting, one tipped globe or seeds held through a cold pause. CELL 11, Mountain range: A continuous serrated chain of three dark ochre mountains rises in overlapping ridges, with pale high peaks and a deep shadowed valley between them. Distinguish: Several linked ridges without erupting crater, broad U-shaped valley focus or a dominant ice tongue. CELL 12, Rain shadow: One sharp mountain divides the circle: a jade cloud rains on its green windward slope while the far slope is bare ochre beneath clear sky; a thin air ribbon passes over the summit. Distinguish: Wet and dry sides of the same barrier are essential; no detached desert panorama or uniform mountain weather. CELL 13, Desert: Broad ochre dunes curve around a patch of cracked stony ground beneath a small white sun, with deep indigo shadows and no water or green plants. Distinguish: Dry open land without wet refuge, grass cover or explanatory mountain comparison. CELL 14, Oasis: A small jade spring-fed pool sits within ochre desert rock, ringed by several dense green shrubs and one spreading tree. The surrounding land remains dry. Distinguish: Isolated water and vegetation in arid ground, without arriving wildlife, grassland herd or extensive soaked ground. CELL 15, Grassland: A broad stand of tall ochre and jade grasses sways across gently rolling open land, with two distinct seed heads in the foreground and no tree canopy. Distinguish: Grass habitat alone; no highlighted soil cycling, animals or bare dunes. CELL 16, Glacier: A thick pale-blue glacier descends between two dark mountain ridges, its cracked ice tongue curving toward a moraine of loose rocks. Distinguish: Confined flowing mountain ice with cracks, not an expanding continental front, falling snow or ice-free carved valley. CELL 17, Valley: A wide U-shaped ochre valley lies between steep rounded walls, with scraped bare rock and a small stream on the broad flat floor; no ice remains in the foreground. Distinguish: Glacially shaped open land trough, without deep sea, dominant ice tongue or repeatedly divided river channels. CELL 18, Braided river: Several bright jade channels split and rejoin around pale gravel bars across a broad mountain valley, with cold blue headwaters visible in the distance. Distinguish: Repeated inland splits and joins over gravel; delta fans into sea and migration adds animals using the corridor. CELL 19, Grazing herds: Three sturdy four-legged grazing animals with short necks, modest horns and dark hoofed feet bend over open grasses, their bodies smaller than the surrounding land. Distinguish: Short-necked herd animals and grazing posture; no sauropod necks, predator stance or pond gathering. CELL 20, Scent tracking: The recurring small pointed-nosed mammal lowers its nose toward a faint ochre scent trail curling along the ground from an unseen animal, with its ears lifted and body following the trail. Distinguish: Nose and airborne trace guide the route; no remembered fruit destination or visually focused primate. Keep the common circle size and painted finish. Anatomical lineages matter: insects have six legs, birds feathered wings, bats membranous finger-supported wings. A depicted early cell is a symbolic magnified view, not a modern laboratory slide. The world is not Earth's recognizable map. People, if listed, have varied warm earth-brown complexions, simplified features and no modern objects. Never add people, plants or animals to a subject that predates them. Do not draw the subject names.
